passages.text: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Moses for the people of Israel.
These are the rules you must give them.
If you buy a Hebrew servant, he must serve you for six years.
In the seventh year, he will go free.
He will not pay anything to go free.
passages.original: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּשִׂ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃ כִּ֤י תִקְנֶה֙ עֶ֣בֶד עִבְרִ֔י שֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים יַעֲבֹ֑ד וּבַ֨שְּׁבִעִ֔ת יֵצֵ֥א לַֽחָפְשִׁ֖י חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.
passages.sermon:
A Hebrew servant may be bought.
He may arrive alone.
If he arrives alone, he must leave alone.
He may arrive with a wife.
If he arrives with a wife, his wife must leave with him.
passages.original: אִם־ בְּגַפּ֥וֹ יָבֹ֖א בְּגַפּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֑א אִם־ בַּ֤עַל אִשָּׁה֙ ה֔וּא וְיָצְאָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
passages.sermon:
A Hebrew servant may receive a wife from his master.
The wife may bear him sons or daughters.
The wife and her children will belong to the master.
The servant will go free alone.
passages.original: אִם־ אֲדֹנָיו֙ יִתֶּן־ ל֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה וְיָלְדָה־ ל֥וֹ בָנִ֖ים א֣וֹ בָנ֑וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וִילָדֶ֗יהָ תִּהְיֶה֙ לַֽאדֹנֶ֔יהָ וְה֖וּא יֵצֵ֥א בְגַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’ then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.
passages.sermon:
A servant may choose to stay with his master.
The servant may say, “I love my master.”
He may also say, “I love my wife and my children.”
He may say, “I do not want to go free.”
The master must bring the servant before the judges.
The master must take the servant to the door or the doorpost.
The master must pierce the servant’s ear with an awl.
The servant will then serve his master for life.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אָמֹ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אָהַ֙בְתִּי֙ אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֔י אֶת־ אִשְׁתִּ֖י וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֑י לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א חָפְשִֽׁי׃ וְהִגִּישׁ֤וֹ אֲדֹנָיו֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהִגִּישׁוֹ֙ אֶל־ הַדֶּ֔לֶת א֖וֹ אֶל־ הַמְּזוּזָ֑ה וְרָצַ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤יו אֶת־ אָזְנוֹ֙ בַּמַּרְצֵ֔עַ וַעֲבָד֖וֹ לְעֹלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.
passages.sermon: A man may sell his daughter as a servant.\r\nShe will not go free in the same way that male servants do.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִמְכֹּ֥ר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־ בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאָמָ֑ה לֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א כְּצֵ֥את הָעֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
passages.sermon:
A man may sell his daughter as a servant.
The master may choose her for himself.
If the master finds her displeasing, he must let her be redeemed.
He cannot sell her to foreigners.
He has broken faith with her.
He has no right to sell her to another nation.
passages.original: אִם־ רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־ לֹא יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ לְעַ֥ם נָכְרִ֛י לֹא־ יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְמָכְרָ֖הּ בְּבִגְדוֹ־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.
passages.sermon: A man may sell his daughter as a servant.\r\nHe may choose her to be a wife for his son.\r\nHe must treat her as he would treat his own daughter.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לִבְנ֖וֹ יִֽיעָדֶ֑נָּה כְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַבָּנ֖וֹת יַעֲשֶׂה־ לָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.
passages.sermon:
A man may take another wife.
He must not reduce the food of his first wife.
He must not reduce the clothing of his first wife.
He must not reduce the marital rights of his first wife.
passages.original: אִם־ אַחֶ֖רֶת יִֽקַּֽח־ ל֑וֹ שְׁאֵרָ֛הּ כְּסוּתָ֥הּ וְעֹנָתָ֖הּ לֹ֥א יִגְרָֽע׃

passages.text: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment.
passages.sermon:
A man may take a female servant as a wife for himself or for his son.
He must provide her with food, clothing, and marital rights.
If he does not give her these three things, she may leave.
She is free to go.
She does not have to pay any money to leave.
passages.original: וְאִם־ שְׁלָ֨שׁ־ אֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לָ֑הּ וְיָצְאָ֥ה חִנָּ֖ם אֵ֥ין כָּֽסֶף׃ס

passages.text: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about murder.
\r\nA person may strike another man.
\r\nIf the man dies, the act is murder.
\r\nThe murderer must be put to death.
\r\nGod commands this punishment for murder.
passages.original: מַכֵּ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ וָמֵ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
passages.sermon:
A man may kill another man without planning it.
He did not wait in ambush.
God allowed this to happen.
God will appoint a place for him.
He may flee to that place.
passages.original: וַאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א צָדָ֔ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אִנָּ֣ה לְיָד֑וֹ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י לְךָ֙ מָק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנ֖וּס שָֽׁמָּה׃ס

passages.text: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.
passages.sermon:
A man may plan to harm his neighbor.
He may act with intention and cunning.
He may try to kill his neighbor on purpose.
If he does this, he is guilty of murder.
He may run to My altar for safety.
Do not let the altar protect him.
Take him away from My altar.
You must put him to death.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָזִ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ עַל־ רֵעֵ֖הוּ לְהָרְג֣וֹ בְעָרְמָ֑ה מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י תִּקָּחֶ֖נּוּ לָמֽוּת׃ס

passages.text: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon: This law speaks about children and their parents.\r\nA person strikes his father or his mother.\r\nThis person must be put to death.
passages.original: וּמַכֵּ֥ה אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel through Moses.
God commanded justice and protection for people.
If a person kidnaps another person, he commits a serious crime.
If the kidnapper sells the victim, he is guilty.
If the kidnapper keeps the victim, he is also guilty.
The kidnapper must be put to death.
passages.original: וְגֹנֵ֨ב אִ֧ישׁ וּמְכָר֛וֹ וְנִמְצָ֥א בְיָד֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃ס

passages.text: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon: Anyone who curses his father must be put to death.\r\nAnyone who curses his mother must be put to death.
passages.original: וּמְקַלֵּ֥ל אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃ס

passages.text: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed, then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
passages.sermon:
Two men may quarrel.
One man may strike the other.
He may use a stone or his fist.
The injured man may not die.
He may be confined to bed.
If the injured man gets up,
If he walks outside with his staff,
The man who struck him is not punished.
The attacker must pay for the injured man’s lost work.
He must also ensure the injured man is completely healed.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יְרִיבֻ֣ן אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְהִכָּה־ אִישׁ֙ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ בְּאֶ֖בֶן א֣וֹ בְאֶגְרֹ֑ף וְלֹ֥א יָמ֖וּת וְנָפַ֥ל לְמִשְׁכָּֽב׃ אִם־ יָק֞וּם וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּח֛וּץ עַל־ מִשְׁעַנְתּ֖וֹ וְנִקָּ֣ה הַמַּכֶּ֑ה רַ֥ק שִׁבְתּ֛וֹ יִתֵּ֖ן וְרַפֹּ֥א יְרַפֵּֽא׃ס

passages.text: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
passages.sermon:
A man may own a male or female servant.
If the man strikes his servant with a rod,
and the servant dies as a result of the blow,
the man must be punished.
The punishment is certain.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת־ עַבְדּ֜וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת־ אֲמָתוֹ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔בֶט וּמֵ֖ת תַּ֣חַת יָד֑וֹ נָקֹ֖ם יִנָּקֵֽם׃

passages.text: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.
passages.sermon:
A man owns a servant.
The man strikes the servant.
The servant does not die.
The servant gets up after a day or two.
The owner will not be punished.
The servant is his property.
passages.original: אַ֥ךְ אִם־ י֛וֹם א֥וֹ יוֹמַ֖יִם יַעֲמֹ֑ד לֹ֣א יֻקַּ֔ם כִּ֥י כַסְפּ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃ס

passages.text: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
passages.sermon:
Two men fight.
They strike a pregnant woman.
Her child is born early.
There is no further injury.
The man who caused this must pay a fine.
The woman’s husband will set the amount.
The court will approve the amount.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִנָּצ֣וּ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְנָ֨גְפ֜וּ אִשָּׁ֤ה הָרָה֙ וְיָצְא֣וּ יְלָדֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה אָס֑וֹן עָנ֣וֹשׁ יֵעָנֵ֗שׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׁ֤ית עָלָיו֙ בַּ֣עַל הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנָתַ֖ן בִּפְלִלִֽים׃

passages.text: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life— eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel about justice and fairness.
If someone causes a serious injury to another person, the punishment must fit the harm done.
If someone takes a life, then a life must be given in return.
If someone destroys an eye, then an eye must be given in return.
If someone knocks out a tooth, then a tooth must be given in return.
If someone injures a hand, then a hand must be given in return.
If someone injures a foot, then a foot must be given in return.
If someone causes a burn, then a burn must be given in return.
If someone causes a wound, then a wound must be given in return.
If someone causes a stripe or bruise, then a stripe or bruise must be given in return.
God required equal justice for all people.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אָס֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֥ה נֶ֖פֶשׁ תַּ֥חַת נָֽפֶשׁ׃ עַ֚יִן תַּ֣חַת עַ֔יִן שֵׁ֖ן תַּ֣חַת שֵׁ֑ן יָ֚ד תַּ֣חַת יָ֔ד רֶ֖גֶל תַּ֥חַת רָֽגֶל׃ כְּוִיָּה֙ תַּ֣חַת כְּוִיָּ֔ה פֶּ֖צַע תַּ֣חַת פָּ֑צַע חַבּוּרָ֕ה תַּ֖חַת חַבּוּרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
passages.sermon:
A man may have a male servant or a female servant.
If the man strikes his servant’s eye, he may cause injury.
If the servant’s eye is blinded, the servant suffers loss.
The man must let the servant go free.
The freedom is compensation for the loss of the eye.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־ עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־ אֶת־ עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת עֵינֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
passages.sermon:
A man owns a male or female servant.
If the man knocks out the tooth of his servant,
he must let the servant go free.
The servant goes free as compensation for the lost tooth.
passages.original: וְאִם־ שֵׁ֥ן עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־ שֵׁ֥ן אֲמָת֖וֹ יַפִּ֑יל לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת שִׁנּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.
passages.sermon:
An ox is a large, domesticated animal.
If an ox gores a man to death, the ox must be stoned.
If an ox gores a woman to death, the ox must be stoned.
No one may eat the meat of the ox.
The owner of the ox is not guilty.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת־ אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת־ אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת־ בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וּבַ֥עַל הַשּׁ֖וֹר נָקִֽי׃

passages.text: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
passages.sermon:
This law concerns an ox that is dangerous and its owner who is responsible.
The ox has a habit of goring people.
The owner has been warned about the ox before.
The owner does not keep the ox under control.
The ox kills a man or a woman.
People must stone the ox to death.
People must also put the owner of the ox to death.
passages.original: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם־ בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.
passages.sermon:
The law concerns an ox that kills a person.
The owner of the ox is responsible if he was warned and did not restrain the ox.
If the owner is sentenced to death, a payment may be demanded instead.
If payment is demanded, the owner may pay the full amount required.
By paying, the owner redeems his life.
passages.original: אִם־ כֹּ֖פֶר יוּשַׁ֣ת עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַן֙ פִּדְיֹ֣ן נַפְשׁ֔וֹ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יוּשַׁ֖ת עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
passages.sermon:
An ox may gore a son.
An ox may gore a daughter.
The same rule applies in both cases.
The owner must face the same judgment as in other cases of goring.
The law does not change because the victim is a son or a daughter.
passages.original: אוֹ־ בֵ֥ן יִגָּ֖ח אוֹ־ בַ֣ת יִגָּ֑ח כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט הַזֶּ֖ה יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.
passages.sermon:
This law concerns an ox that kills a servant.
A servant can be a manservant or a maidservant.
If an ox gores a manservant or a maidservant, the servant dies.
The owner of the ox must pay money.
The owner must pay thirty shekels of silver.
The owner must give this money to the master of the servant.
The ox must be stoned to death.
passages.original: אִם־ עֶ֛בֶד יִגַּ֥ח הַשּׁ֖וֹר א֣וֹ אָמָ֑ה כֶּ֣סֶף׀ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים יִתֵּן֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔יו וְהַשּׁ֖וֹר יִסָּקֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it, the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
passages.sermon:
A man may open a pit.
A man may dig a pit.
He does not cover the pit.
An ox may fall into the pit.
A donkey may fall into the pit.
The owner of the pit must pay for the loss.
He must give money to the owner of the animal.
The dead animal will belong to the owner of the pit.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי־ יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וְנָֽפַל־ שָׁ֥מָּה שּׁ֖וֹר א֥וֹ חֲמֽוֹר׃ בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־ לּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
passages.sermon:
If a man owns an ox, and that ox injures his neighbor’s ox, and the neighbor’s ox dies, both men must act.
They must sell the ox that is still alive.
They must divide the money from the sale equally.
They must also divide the dead ox equally.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִגֹּ֧ף שֽׁוֹר־ אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־ שׁ֥וֹר רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת וּמָ֨כְר֜וּ אֶת־ הַשּׁ֤וֹר הַחַי֙ וְחָצ֣וּ אֶת־ כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־ הַמֵּ֖ת יֶֽחֱצֽוּן׃

passages.text: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
passages.sermon:
This law concerns an ox that is known to be dangerous.
The ox has a habit of goring.
People knew about this habit before.
The owner of the ox did not restrain it.
The ox killed another ox.
The owner of the dangerous ox must pay full compensation.
He must give another ox in place of the dead ox.
The dead ox will belong to him.
passages.original: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־ לּֽוֹ׃ס
